thm4-reversed-interval.original: Define the interval $\script{B}_j \defequiv [Q_{j, High}, Q_{j, Low}]$. ... Now define $\tilde{\script{B}_j}= \defequiv [Q_{j, High}+\delta_{max}, Q_{j, Low}]$.
thm4-reversed-interval.replacement: Define the interval $\script{B}_j \defequiv [Q_{j, Low}, Q_{j, High}]$. ... Now define $\tilde{\script{B}}_j \defequiv [\max[Q_{j, Low}-\delta_{max}, 0], Q_{j, High}+\delta_{max}]$.
thm4-reversed-interval.reason: Endpoints of B_j and B_tilde_j are written in reverse order (Q_{j,High} >= Q_{j,Low}), and L664 also has a duplicate "= \defequiv" typo; moreover under Eq. (3) service mu_j(t) <= delta_max precedes arrivals A_j(t), so packets arriving at q_j(t) = Q_{j,Low} can land down to max(Q_{j,Low} - delta_max, 0).

thm4-partb-guard-and-width.original: (b) The average delay of these packets is at most $W_{bound}$, where: \[ W_{bound} \defequiv [2D + 2K[\log(V)]^2+\delta_{max}]/\tilde{\lambda}_j. \]
thm4-partb-guard-and-width.replacement: (b) Whenever $\tilde{\lambda}_j > 0$, the average delay of these packets is at most $W_{bound}$, where \[ W_{bound} \defequiv [2D + 2K[\log(V)]^2 + 2\delta_{max} + 1]/\tilde{\lambda}_j \] (assuming discrete unit-size packets under (\ref{eq:queuedynamic}) and almost-surely constant time-average arrival rates $\lambda_j, \tilde{\lambda}_j$).
thm4-partb-guard-and-width.reason: Four formalization findings: (1) Part (a) allows lambda_tilde_j = 0 for small V >= 1, so Part (b) requires an explicit lambda_tilde_j > 0 guard (present in the commented earlier draft at L678); (2) under Eq. (3) service before arrivals shifts the lowest reachable buffer slot down by delta_max, adding +delta_max to the window width; (3) counting integer buffer slots in a real interval adds +1 from endpoint rounding; (4) the DCT step at L641-L648 requires almost-surely constant (ergodic) time-average limits, not merely a.s. existence.
